feedback: Strong capstone from Jahmir, near the top of the cohort, with real gaps that keep it out of the 80s. On D1 the catalogue is broad and the evidence is mostly quoted: SQL injection is nailed with the concatenated WHERE clause and A03/CWE-89, the unsalted MD5 is named (CWE-328 is a fine variant of 916), alg:none is correctly A07, and the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 is quoted. The decoy is the best part of the submission. You correctly identify the hash_equals construct as safe, prove it constant-time at the mechanism level, and you do not fall into the trap of calling alg:none the decoy, which earns full marks on that row. What costs you on D1 is that XXE never appears in the findings catalogue itself, it only shows up later in the chain, so finding 7 is effectively absent from the D1 deliverable, and a couple of evidence lines (the MD5 line around 66 and the 02:18:47 XSS cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9) are described rather than quoted. On D2 the chain is in the right order and each hop carries a specific PoC, with 02:15:31 SQLi, 02:16:04 bulk PII of 312 rows, 02:18:47 XSS, 02:21:13 open redirect, and 02:24:02 file read all reconciled. Two things hold the row down: you scored SQLi as A:L giving 9.8 when the bypass does not touch availability, so the correct vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1, and the impact section never converts 312 customers into a naira figure or names the senior insight that a forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, which is the scope change S:C that makes this severe. On D3 the report reads well, the threat model is clear, findings are tied to capture lines, the decoy is restated correctly, and crucially you order remediation by effort to risk rather than by CVSS, which is exactly what was asked. The executive headline is garbled, ₦78 million dollars mixes currencies and reads as an error, and your detection stopgaps give field-specific regex but only qualitative Low and Very low false-positive language instead of a rate. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice and cites ISC2 canons I and II by number in a load-bearing way, anchored to the 312 records and the JWT and XML findings, but you name the NDPA 2023 duty only in prose and never cite section 40 (notify NDPC within 72 hours) or section 41 (notify data subjects on high risk), which was a load-bearing requirement. I looked hard for a way to push this into the high 70s and accepted your CWE variants and your prose findings to get there, but the missing XXE entry in D1, the absent naira impact in D2, and the missing NDPA sections genuinely cap it where it sits. The single most important fix is to finish the impact story end to end: state the naira exposure across the 312 customers with your assumptions, tie it to BoltCash and the six week launch window, and cite NDPA sections 40 and 41 by number so the business consequence is as concrete as your technical evidence.
